result.topic_en: A heuristic derivation, assuming the prime number theorem, that the sum of log p/(p-1) over primes p<x equals log x minus Euler's constant plus o(1), via the behaviour of zeta-type Dirichlet series as s tends to 1.
result.transcription:
As $s \to 1$
$\Sigma \frac{1}{n^s} = \frac{1}{s-1} + \gamma + o(1)$
$\Sigma \frac{\log n}{n^s} = \frac{1}{(s-1)^2} + K + o(1)$
Hence $\frac{\Sigma \frac{\log n}{n^s}}{\Sigma \frac{1}{n^s}} = \frac{1}{s-1} - \gamma + o(1)$
But $\frac{\Sigma \frac{\log n}{n^s}}{\Sigma \frac{1}{n^s}} \equiv \Sigma \frac{\log p}{p^s - 1}$
$\therefore \Sigma \frac{\log p}{p^s-1} = \frac{1}{s-1} - \gamma + o(1)$
(1) So that $\Sigma \frac{1}{n^s} - \Sigma \frac{\log p}{p^s-1} = 2\gamma + o(1)$.
(2) But $\Sigma_{n<x} \frac{1}{n} = \log x + \gamma + o(1)$.
$\therefore$ Assuming $\pi(x) \sim \frac{x}{\log x}$ we have
(3) $\Sigma_{p<x} \frac{\log p}{p-1} = \log x + B + o(1)$.
Hence from (1), (2) and (3)
$\gamma - B = 2\gamma$
that is $B = -\gamma$
Hence we have
$\frac{\log 2}{2-1} + \frac{\log 3}{3-1} + \frac{\log 5}{5-1} + \frac{\log 7}{7-1} \cdots + \frac{\log p}{p-1} \quad p<x$
$= \log x - \gamma + o(1)$.

items.english: Assuming pi(x) ~ x/log x, we have that the sum over primes p<x of log p/(p-1) equals log x + B + o(1).
The sum log2/(2-1) + log3/(3-1) + ... + log p/(p-1) over p<x equals log x - gamma + o(1).
